Rationale: Floor is 100, not 0: a worn person always logs incidental steps, so 0-99 = non-wear/error. Upper is the pregnancy-cohort standard.
Inspire 3 has NO onboard GPS: distance = steps x stride, so it is bounded by the step cap. 60 km ~= 45,000 steps at a long running stride. Confirm km vs miles.
Basis: Derived from step cap + device (no GPS)

Rationale: 0 is a REAL value in pregnancy (MVPA is low and declining; typical <30 min/day). Upper is a loose gross-error cap.
Very low LPA on a worn day is unusual but is caught by the wear-time day filter, not a hard floor here.
Cannot exceed the day. ~1440 combined with steps<100 and no HR = non-wear -> drop the DAY (see Day-validity).
Total EE must be >= BMR. AoU median BMR ~1,474 kcal, median total EE ~2,100 kcal; <1000 => non-wear/error.
0 plausible on a sedentary day; upper is a gross-error cap.
Athletic lows reach ~35. Pregnancy shifts RHR UP (+10-20 bpm); sustained resting >120 or <35 = error/pathology.
Hard bound = 0-24 h. Do NOT null short nights at value level; instead apply the PERSON-level rule (see Day-validity): exclude if >30% of days <240 min (4 h).
Basis: AoU pregnancy Fitbit study (0-24 h; <4 h rule)

Rationale: 0-24 h. Must be >= total minutes asleep (see Consistency).
Stage-classified nights only. Stage-sum check does the real validation.
Data-quality/nap indicator, not an exposure. >1 flags naps/fragmentation to reconcile.
